paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of and by language family. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect of different multilingual BERT models across various language families, as measured by a quantitative metric labeled "effect" on the vertical axis. The horizontal axis categorizes language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. For each language family, four grouped bars are displayed, corresponding to the models: mBERT-targ (light blue), XLM-targ (dark blue), mBERT-permute (light green), and XLM-permute (dark green), as indicated in the legend. The vertical axis is scaled linearly from 0 to 40, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Error bars extending above and below each bar represent the standard deviation of the effect. In general, the mBERT-targ and XLM-targ models show higher effect values compared to their permuted counterparts (mBERT-permute and XLM-permute) across all language families. The highest effect values are observed in the "Isolate" and "Uralic" families, particularly for mBERT-targ (around 35) and XLM-targ (around 25), while the permuted models show minimal effects in these groups (near 0). The bars are arranged in groups by language family, with consistent color coding for each model across all families. There is no explicit sorting of language families by effect; they appear in a fixed order from left to right. The chart does not highlight any specific bars with additional annotations or shading.
